objective: Fix the job pipeline timeout defect so the producer-set timeout reaches downstream consumers: job_timeout in pipeline/consumer.py resolves the frozen wire key timeout_ms first (draft 'timeout' key kept only as a deprecated fallback), producer and engine stay unchanged, every existing test case remains green unmodified, and tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py goes fully green.
in_scope: Explicit, frozen decision of which side adapts to the wire contract (recorded as DA-1: the consumer side adapts)
Change job_timeout in pipeline/consumer.py to resolve timeout_ms (authoritative) -> 'timeout' (deprecated fallback) -> DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000)
Add unit tests in tests/test_consumer.py covering the resolution order (additive only; existing test cases untouched)
Add e2e seam regression tests in tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py (additive only; existing test cases untouched)
Whole test suite green: tests/test_producer.py, tests/test_consumer.py, tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py (pytest exit code 0)

out_of_scope.item: Removing the draft 'timeout' key fallback from consumer.job_timeout
out_of_scope.reason: removal changes observable behavior for legacy jobs and would break the existing green unit test that pins the draft key; defer to a later Stage once all producers are known to emit only timeout_ms

out_of_scope.item: Any change to pipeline/producer.py (key rename, signature, default value)
out_of_scope.reason: producer's timeout_ms is the frozen reference wire contract per DA-1; renaming on the producer side would also force engine and 2 green producer unit tests to change, violating 'do not rename keys on both sides'

out_of_scope.item: Any change to pipeline/engine.py semantics (comparison operator, status literals, default)
out_of_scope.reason: task constraint: do not change the simulated carrier/engine semantics beyond the fix; engine already consumes the wire key and is green

out_of_scope.item: Introducing a real transport/serialization layer between producer, engine, and consumer
out_of_scope.reason: the simulated pass-through job dict is the carrier; adding a serializer changes carrier semantics beyond the fix

out_of_scope.item: Extending consumer.validate_job (e.g. type-checking timeout_ms, range checks)
out_of_scope.reason: validate_job is not part of the defect; changing it alters a behavior no in-scope task needs and would add a new contract obligation

frozen_assumptions.statement: The job dict is the wire carrier: producer, engine, and consumer exchange the same dict object with no serializer in between
frozen_assumptions.rationale: tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py passes producer.make_job output directly to consumer.job_timeout and engine.run_job; no encoding layer exists anywhere in the repo

frozen_assumptions.statement: timeout_ms and work_ms are integers in the same unit (milliseconds)
frozen_assumptions.rationale: field names and the engine comparison (work_ms > timeout_ms) plus the e2e expectations (timeout_ms=100 with work_ms 50 -> done, 150 -> timeout) are consistent only under one shared unit

frozen_assumptions.statement: Every job in this system is emitted by producer.make_job and therefore carries timeout_ms; the draft 'timeout' key has no in-repo emitter
frozen_assumptions.rationale: only consumer.py references the 'timeout' key; keeping it as a fallback is migration tolerance, not a live dual contract, so the fallback cannot mask a second wire format

frozen_assumptions.statement: The baseline failure is exactly one test (test_pipeline_e2e_effective_timeout, consumer job_timeout returns 30000 instead of 500) and all other tests pass
frozen_assumptions.rationale: verified by running the suite on the baseline fixture: '1 failed, 6 passed'; the task statement and the e2e file docstring agree with this result

frozen_architecture.decision: The consumer side adapts to the wire contract: timeout_ms (the producer's key) is the authoritative timeout field on the wire; the consumer's draft 'timeout' key is demoted to a deprecated, lower-priority fallback. No key is renamed on the producer side or the engine side, and no job is ever written with both keys by this stage.
frozen_architecture.rationale: producer's timeout_ms is documented as the producer contract, is already consumed by engine, and is pinned by 2 green producer unit tests plus the green engine e2e case; the consumer's 'timeout' key is explicitly a draft (consumer.py NOTE) with no in-repo emitter. Consumer-side adaptation satisfies the task's mandatory decision, keeps every existing unit test green with zero test edits (the fallback preserves test_job_timeout_reads_consumer_key), and leaves engine semantics untouched.

frozen_architecture.decision: The code fix is confined to pipeline/consumer.py; test work is additive-only in tests/test_consumer.py and tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py. No new modules, no package layout change, no new dependencies.
frozen_architecture.rationale: smallest diff that implements DA-1; keeps the defect locally recoverable (a failed leaf invalidates only its own files) and preserves the green baseline for everything outside the seam

shared_contracts.spec: Job wire schema (pre-existing, frozen): producer.make_job(job_id, payload, timeout_ms=30000) returns exactly {'id': <job_id>, 'payload': <payload>, 'timeout_ms': <int ms>}; timeout_ms is the authoritative timeout key on the wire. Engine consumes it via job.get('timeout_ms', 30000) with the strict comparison work_ms > timeout_ms -> status 'timeout', else status 'done'. Producer and engine behavior is frozen as-is for this stage; any change to the job dict shape, key names, or the engine comparison is out of scope.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: any change to the job dict shape, key names, defaults, or engine comparison is a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST decided by the planning layer

shared_contracts.spec: Consumer timeout resolution (frozen by DA-1): job_timeout(job) returns job['timeout_ms'] if that key is present, else job['timeout'] (deprecated draft key, fallback only) if that key is present, else DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000). validate_job is unchanged: it raises ValueError when 'id' or 'payload' is missing and returns True otherwise. DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS stays defined in pipeline/consumer.py with value 30000.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: any change to the resolution order, the fallback policy, or validate_job semantics is a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST

integration_seams.description: Producer -> consumer wire hand-off: the job dict from producer.make_job is parsed by consumer.job_timeout / consumer.validate_job; the timeout defect lives exactly at this seam (timeout_ms emitted, draft 'timeout' expected)
Producer -> engine wire hand-off: the job dict from producer.make_job is executed by engine.run_job; already consistent (both sides use timeout_ms) and frozen unchanged in this stage

acceptance.description: Consumer returns the producer-set timeout at the S1 seam (the baseline defect is that it returns the default 30000 instead)
acceptance.negative_case: a job dict with no timeout_ms but timeout=123 -> job_timeout returns 123 (deprecated fallback); a job dict with neither key -> job_timeout returns 30000 (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS)
acceptance.failure_behavior: if timeout_ms is not honored, job_timeout returns 30000 for the positive case and pytest fails test_pipeline_e2e_effective_timeout with assertion 30000 != 500, exactly as in the baseline

acceptance.description: Full suite green with zero modifications to existing test cases (additive tests only)
acceptance.positive_case: python -m pytest tests/ from the repo root exits 0 with all producer, consumer, and e2e tests passing, including the new regression tests
acceptance.negative_case: any existing test case modified, removed, or skipped fails acceptance even when the pytest exit code is 0 (checked by diff of the three pre-existing test files' original cases)
acceptance.failure_behavior: pytest exits non-zero; the failing test name localizes the defect to T01 (consumer resolution) or to a T02 regression case, so one leaf's failure invalidates only its own subgraph
acceptance.evidence: pytest tests/ -> exit code 0, 0 failed (baseline: exactly 1 failed, 6 passed)

acceptance.description: Engine returns unchanged statuses at the S2 seam (frozen): work_ms above timeout_ms -> status 'timeout', work_ms at or below -> status 'done'
acceptance.positive_case: engine.run_job(job with timeout_ms=100, work_ms=50) returns {'id': 'j2', 'status': 'done'}; engine.run_job(job with timeout_ms=100, work_ms=150) returns status 'timeout'
acceptance.negative_case: work_ms equal to timeout_ms (100 vs 100) returns status 'done' because the frozen comparison is strict (work_ms > timeout_ms)
acceptance.failure_behavior: any change to the comparison, the status literals, or the default in pipeline/engine.py or pipeline/producer.py raises a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST (C-class), not an inline fix
acceptance.evidence: pytest tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py::TestPipelineE2E::test_pipeline_e2e_engine_timeout -> passed; diff of pipeline/ shows producer.py and engine.py unmodified

constraints.rule: exactly one side adapts to the wire key (the consumer, per DA-1); renaming keys on both sides - e.g. switching producer to emit 'timeout' - is forbidden
pipeline/engine.py and pipeline/producer.py must be byte-identical at stage close (no semantic or cosmetic change)
no new dependencies; stdlib plus the existing test runner (unittest/pytest) only
existing test methods stay byte-identical; all new tests are additive (new test methods inside the existing test files)

resource_budget.stage_estimate: 2-4 dev-hours (two small sequential leaves plus verification)

open_questions.question: Which side adapts to the wire contract - the producer's timeout_ms or the consumer's draft 'timeout' key?
open_questions.resolution: resolved in this contract by frozen decision DA-1: the consumer side adapts - timeout_ms becomes the authoritative wire key, the draft 'timeout' key is kept only as a deprecated lower-priority fallback; rationale recorded on DA-1 (producer key is the documented contract, already consumed by engine and pinned by 3 green tests; consumer key is an explicitly drafted, emitter-less key)
